tool.name: chainMergeSort
tool.description: : combine sorted chain files into one sorted chain file
tool.command: ## ⛔ THE FILE LIST GOES IN A FILE, NOT ON THE COMMAND LINE. This tool exists to collapse an axis ## that a pairwise workflow maps over, so the input is routinely a collection with one element per ## chromosome pair -- a few hundred paths, each a long Galaxy dataset path. `chainMergeSort a b c ## ...` would work until a panel got wide enough to hit ARG_MAX, and then fail on the size of the ## panel rather than on anything about the data. `-inputList` is the option upstream provides for ## exactly this and has no downside. #for $chain in $in_chains: echo '$chain' >> input_list.txt && #end for chainMergeSort -inputList=input_list.txt -tempDir=./ > '$out'

param.name: in_chains
param.label: Chain datasets to merge
param.help: Each input must already be sorted by score -- this is a merge, not a sort. In a pairwise pipeline that means one chainSort (or one axtChain, whose output is score-ordered) per element upstream of here.

tool.help:
**What it does**
`chainMergeSort`_ combines several chain files that are each already sorted by score into one file sorted by score. It is a k-way merge: it streams its inputs rather than loading them, which is why ``chainSort``'s own documentation points here for anything large.
**Why a pairwise pipeline needs it**
A whole-genome alignment can be computed one chromosome pair at a time, which is what lets Galaxy run the expensive stages in parallel. The chain/net stages that follow cannot be partitioned that way: ``chainPreNet`` and ``chainNet`` each walk one score-ordered stream marking target and query space *simultaneously*, so a chain on ``(tchr1, qchr5)`` competes with one on ``(tchr3, qchr5)``. This tool is where the per-chromosome-pair axis collapses back into one stream, and its output -- score-ordered -- is exactly ``chainPreNet``'s precondition, so it replaces a final ``chainSort`` rather than adding a pass.
.. class:: warningmark
**The ids are renumbered, and that is the point.** Independent ``axtChain`` runs each number their chains from 1, so chunks arriving here carry colliding ids -- and ``netChainSubset`` matches nets to chains **by id**. Renumbering is what repairs that. Upstream offers a ``-saveId`` flag to keep the existing ids; this wrapper deliberately does not expose it, because on the one workflow shape that makes this tool necessary, the flag that sounds conservative is the one that corrupts the result.
For implementation details see chainMergeSort's `source code`_.
.. _chainMergeSort: http://hgdownload.cse.ucsc.edu/admin/exe/linux.x86_64/FOOTER.txt .. _source code: https://github.com/ucscGenomeBrowser/kent/blob/master/src/hg/mouseStuff/chainMergeSort/chainMergeSort.c
